article.title: ペーパードライバー
article.part: Contraste Guatemala–Japón — グアテマラと日本語の対照
article.chapter: Préstamos engañosos y equivalencias falsas — 紛らわしい外来語・偽の対応

claims.summary: ペーパードライバー is a Japanese expression for a person who holds a driver’s license but does not actually drive; dictionaries label paper driver as Japanese usage.
Imidas distinguishes Japanese ペーパードライバー from English Sunday driver, which it defines as a person who drives only on days off such as Sundays.
Seisen Nihon Kokugo Daijiten cites a 1961 example of ペーパー・ドライバー, glossed as a licensed person who has no car.
The dictionaries inspected define license-holding non-driving but do not specify a time threshold or assess driving ability.

locator.description: コトバンク, 小学館「デジタル大辞泉」, lines 14–21: Japanese usage, license holder who does not actually drive; 「精選版 日本国語大辞典」, lines 25–31: license holder who does not drive a car.

links.notes: The Spanish description follows the dictionary wording.
